lines.text: A single coral island in the Pacific, the smallest republic in the world, that grew rich on its own rock and then lost it. This is Nauru.
For a long time twelve clans shared the island. Then traders brought guns, and from 1878 a war between clans raged for ten years.
Germany took the island, and in 1906 miners began digging its phosphate. They would strip most of Nauru bare.
Hammer DeRoburt would grow up to lead his people to independence, and win back control of the phosphate.
In the Second World War Japan occupied the island from 1942 to 1945, hard years for the islanders.
Baron Waqa would one day serve as president, from 2013 to 2019.
In 1968 Nauru became independent, and for a time its people were among the richest on Earth.
Marcus Stephen, a weightlifter, won Commonwealth gold, and later became president of his island.
David Adeang, born the same year, would become president in 2023.
But the phosphate ran out, and the wealth went with it. In 2001 Australia opened a camp for asylum seekers on the island.
A tiny island that gave away its ground, Nauru is still searching for its future.
